answer: Sybil resistance here comes from a compute bond per seat, not a registrable claim. Each identity posts a costly proof tied to the epoch seed before earning anything, scored against wallet history, not a fresh address. Cloning means paying that bill on every clone in one window, since rewards stay locked like a vault until settlement. A split-off identity filing contradictory proofs loses its reserve, so faking burns capital and GPU time, and a proof bought for one yarrow seed expires when the seed rotates. One walnut of honest work cannot be split across ten wallets without multiplying cost.
